```text
# #2020: Patch: Infinite Reserves' normal face draws a card when it is played
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Infinite Reserves is a free card, but it only does something once your deck has run out. In a normal game that happens around turn 40, long after most games are over. So in most games it is a blank card that also takes up one of your back-row slots, and the numbers agree: it wins less often than any other card in the game.

Once this is built, playing it also draws you a card, so it replaces itself. Its run-out-of-cards safety net stays as it is, and its upgraded (Radiant) form, which already draws three, is unchanged. Players who choose it, or are dealt it in a random deck, are no longer handed a dead card.

## Why
- The win-rate table the game ships (`crates/cards/data/win_rates.json`, patch v0.4.0, `"source": "provisional"`, 396 cards) has `core-075` at 7 wins in 43 games, 16.3%.
  - That is the lowest of all 396 cards, about 4.4 standard deviations below 50%.
  - The next lowest is `classic-037` at 14 of 47 (29.8%).
- The AI's dealt-quality table, a separate sample, also puts it below its prior: `("core-075", 0.5961)` at `crates/ai/src/shadow_ban.rs:1007`.
- The base face is only the replacement: "Drawing from an empty deck gives you a Rush Token card instead of fatigue." (`catalog.json`; `crates/cards/src/scripts/core/c075_infinite_reserves.rs`; SPEC §8.3 row 75.) The `draw` param exists only for the Radiant Cry.
- SPEC §2.5: "one draw a turn empties a 25-card deck on each player's 21st turn", that is player-turn 41 or 42. The one recorded sample of game lengths, `analysis/fixtures/games.report.json` (40 games of v0.2.5f, before the deck grew from 20 to 25 cards), has quartiles of 12, 15 and 19 turns. So the base face almost never fires.
- In the meantime it sits on the backrow as a public, permanent Field Spell (SPEC §3.2), taking a zone.
- Hearthstone's answer for a situational effect on a cheap card is a cantrip: it draws one, so it costs no card.

## Proposal
- Give the base face "Cry: Draw {draw}." on top of the replacement. The `draw` param's base value becomes 1 and the Radiant value stays 3, so the Radiant upgrade still moves the number up (R386). The Radiant face's text and behaviour are unchanged.
- Update the script and its header comment, the catalog text (English and zh-CN), SPEC §8.3 row 75 (including its Tunes cell) and BUILD's must-pass row for #75.
- Write the pending fragment with `cargo jackioh patches "<title>"`. Claim every card that plays differently, NA Tech and CN Tech among them, since they read the win-rate table and fuse or offer this card (R1366000). Hold the claims to `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`.
- Quote the measured effect in the fragment's notes, as docs/issues-and-patches.md "Win rates in a balance patch" says (R1284000):
  - a forced run on a worktree of the base commit and another on the branch;
  - then `cargo jackioh stats compare --card core-075`, quoting both rates, the paired difference and their intervals.

## Where it lands
- `crates/cards/src/scripts/core/c075_infinite_reserves.rs`
- `crates/cards/catalog.json` and the zh-CN card text
- a new pending fragment under `crates/cards/patches/`
- `spec/08-catalog.md` §8.3 row 75 and `BUILD.md`'s #75 row
- possibly the tests that use Infinite Reserves as a Field Spell that does nothing, for example:
  - `classic/c025_lag_in_the_system.rs:107`
  - `classic_plus/c020_mushroom_power.rs:51` ("which touches no Unit")
  - `core/c050_k_pop_fanatic.rs:1110`
  - `meditative/c071_pareto_optimality.rs:255`

  Only where one of them plays the card from hand rather than placing it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The card's tests:
  - the base face played from hand draws exactly one card;
  - a draw from an empty library still gives a Rush Token card instead of fatigue, on both faces;
  - the Radiant face still draws 3 and keeps the replacement;
  - upgrading and degrading move the number between 1 and 3 (R386).
- [ ] These pass: `cargo test -p jackioh-cards`; the engine's rule tests with `testkit`; `cargo jackioh catalog check`; `cargo jackioh patches check`; `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`; `cargo jackioh spec check`. The golden replay still passes, because a replay folds under its pinned catalog (R767000).
- [ ] The fragment's notes quote `stats compare` for core-075 with both rates, the paired difference and their intervals.
- [ ] SPEC §8.3 row 75, the catalog text and the script header say the same thing.

## Size and risks
Small to medium: one card, its text, the spec row and a fragment. It ships a version through `patches ship`.

Risks:
- The evidence is one provisional AI-against-AI table (43 games of this card) plus the AI's own dealt-quality number, so the forced `stats compare` is what confirms it.
- A free card that draws feeds effects that count plays or cards drawn.
- NA Tech's fused card changes with it.
- The designer may prefer another fix, such as a different base effect. The issue thread is the place to say so before the bot builds it.

# #2020: Patch: Infinite Reserves' normal face draws a card when it is played
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means
Infinite Reserves is a free card, but it only does something once your deck has run out. In a normal game that happens around turn 40, long after most games are over. So in most games it is a blank card that also takes up one of your back-row slots, and the numbers agree: it wins less often than any other card in the game.

Once this is built, playing it also draws you a card, so it replaces itself. Its run-out-of-cards safety net stays as it is, and its upgraded (Radiant) form, which already draws three, is unchanged. Players who choose it, or are dealt it in a random deck, are no longer handed a dead card.

## Why
- The win-rate table the game ships (`crates/cards/data/win_rates.json`, patch v0.4.0, `"source": "provisional"`, 396 cards) has `core-075` at 7 wins in 43 games, 16.3%.
  - That is the lowest of all 396 cards, about 4.4 standard deviations below 50%.
  - The next lowest is `classic-037` at 14 of 47 (29.8%).
- The AI's dealt-quality table, a separate sample, also puts it below its prior: `("core-075", 0.5961)` at `crates/ai/src/shadow_ban.rs:1007`.
- The base face is only the replacement: "Drawing from an empty deck gives you a Rush Token card instead of fatigue." (`catalog.json`; `crates/cards/src/scripts/core/c075_infinite_reserves.rs`; SPEC §8.3 row 75.) The `draw` param exists only for the Radiant Cry.
- SPEC §2.5: "one draw a turn empties a 25-card deck on each player's 21st turn", that is player-turn 41 or 42. The one recorded sample of game lengths, `analysis/fixtures/games.report.json` (40 games of v0.2.5f, before the deck grew from 20 to 25 cards), has quartiles of 12, 15 and 19 turns. So the base face almost never fires.
- In the meantime it sits on the backrow as a public, permanent Field Spell (SPEC §3.2), taking a zone.
- Hearthstone's answer for a situational effect on a cheap card is a cantrip: it draws one, so it costs no card.

## Proposal
- Give the base face "Cry: Draw {draw}." on top of the replacement. The `draw` param's base value becomes 1 and the Radiant value stays 3, so the Radiant upgrade still moves the number up (R386). The Radiant face's text and behaviour are unchanged.
- Update the script and its header comment, the catalog text (English and zh-CN), SPEC §8.3 row 75 (including its Tunes cell) and BUILD's must-pass row for #75.
- Write the pending fragment with `cargo jackioh patches "<title>"`. Claim every card that plays differently, NA Tech and CN Tech among them, since they read the win-rate table and fuse or offer this card (R1366000). Hold the claims to `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`.
- Quote the measured effect in the fragment's notes, as docs/issues-and-patches.md "Win rates in a balance patch" says (R1284000):
  - a forced run on a worktree of the base commit and another on the branch;
  - then `cargo jackioh stats compare --card core-075`, quoting both rates, the paired difference and their intervals.

## Where it lands
- `crates/cards/src/scripts/core/c075_infinite_reserves.rs`
- `crates/cards/catalog.json` and the zh-CN card text
- a new pending fragment under `crates/cards/patches/`
- `spec/08-catalog.md` §8.3 row 75 and `BUILD.md`'s #75 row
- possibly the tests that use Infinite Reserves as a Field Spell that does nothing, for example:
  - `classic/c025_lag_in_the_system.rs:107`
  - `classic_plus/c020_mushroom_power.rs:51` ("which touches no Unit")
  - `core/c050_k_pop_fanatic.rs:1110`
  - `meditative/c071_pareto_optimality.rs:255`

  Only where one of them plays the card from hand rather than placing it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The card's tests:
  - the base face played from hand draws exactly one card;
  - a draw from an empty library still gives a Rush Token card instead of fatigue, on both faces;
  - the Radiant face still draws 3 and keeps the replacement;
  - upgrading and degrading move the number between 1 and 3 (R386).
- [ ] These pass: `cargo test -p jackioh-cards`; the engine's rule tests with `testkit`; `cargo jackioh catalog check`; `cargo jackioh patches check`; `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims`; `cargo jackioh spec check`. The golden replay still passes, because a replay folds under its pinned catalog (R767000).
- [ ] The fragment's notes quote `stats compare` for core-075 with both rates, the paired difference and their intervals.
- [ ] SPEC §8.3 row 75, the catalog text and the script header say the same thing.

## Size and risks
Small to medium: one card, its text, the spec row and a fragment. It ships a version through `patches ship`.

Risks:
- The evidence is one provisional AI-against-AI table (43 games of this card) plus the AI's own dealt-quality number, so the forced `stats compare` is what confirms it.
- A free card that draws feeds effects that count plays or cards drawn.
- NA Tech's fused card changes with it.
- The designer may prefer another fix, such as a different base effect. The issue thread is the place to say so before the bot builds it.
